tier_reason: The kostya/benchmarks Json table has every quoted row, and the harness is public (json/json.rs/src/json_struct.rs, json_pull.rs and json_value.rs against json/test_rapid.cpp and test_nlohmann_json.cpp; flags in common/commands.mk and json/Makefile; Xeon E-2324G), but the win over RapidJSON and nlohmann/json comes from unequal work (typed decoding that skips name and opts against full DOM builds; the like-for-like serde_json::Value row is 2.9x-3.6x slower than RapidJSON) and from C++ baselines built without -DNDEBUG or RapidJSON SIMD, so it is capped at C, matching the tier given to the same rows in wave14 (lang:rust/kostya/benchmarks#json). The record's compiler versions were also wrong: these rows date from the 2025-08-17 run.

corrections.claimed_speedup: kostya/benchmarks Json table (medians; rows measured in the 2025-08-17 update and carried unchanged into the README dated 2026-07-19): Rust Serde Typed 0.110 s vs C++ RapidJSON 0.154 s (g++) and 0.194 s (clang++), RapidJSON Precise 0.212 s (g++) and 0.262 s (clang++), and nlohmann/json 1.266 s (g++) and 1.182 s (clang++). That is about 1.4x-1.8x faster than default RapidJSON, 1.9x-2.4x faster than RapidJSON Precise and 10.7x-11.5x faster than nlohmann/json (derived from page data). Rust Serde Custom (derive plus a hand-written visitor that folds the array without storing it) takes 0.103 s. Not faster than simdjson On-Demand 0.060 s (g++) / 0.062 s (clang++) or DAW JSON Link 0.085 s (clang++) / 0.089 s (g++); about equal to simdjson DOM 0.103 s (clang++) / 0.107 s (g++). The like-for-like DOM row, Rust Serde Untyped (serde_json::Value) at 0.557 s, is about 2.1x-2.3x faster than nlohmann/json but about 2.9x-3.6x slower than RapidJSON DOM (derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Measured toolchain (the Json rows date from the 2025-08-17 update, kostya/benchmarks commit 63ffa65, and are identical in the 2026-07-19 README, whose Versions table lists newer compilers that did not produce them): Rust 1.89.0, cargo build --release with RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native -C llvm-args=--x86-branches-within-32B-boundaries' and profile.release lto=true, codegen-units=1, panic=abort, strip=true (edition 2024); json.rs/Cargo.lock at that commit pinned serde_json 1.0.142 and serde/serde_derive 1.0.219, with no float_roundtrip feature. C++ baselines: g++ 14.2.0 and clang++ 19.1.7 (clang++ with -stdlib=libc++), -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Wcast-align -O3 -march=native -flto=auto -Wa,-mbranches-within-32B-boundaries -std=c++23 and no -DNDEBUG; RapidJSON built without RAPIDJSON_SSE2 or RAPIDJSON_SSE42; RapidJSON (miloyip/rapidjson), nlohmann/json and simdjson shallow-cloned from master at build time (json/Makefile, common/commands.mk).
corrections.hardware: Intel(R) Xeon(R) E-2324G; Docker image based on Debian GNU/Linux trixie/sid at the 2025-08-17 measurement (the 2026-07-19 README's Environment section now says forky/sid, but the Json rows for Rust, RapidJSON and nlohmann/json were not re-measured then).
corrections.workload: Parse a generated, pretty-printed JSON file (json/generate_json.rb: 524,288 objects, each with x, y and z doubles, a name string and an opts object holding a one-element array, plus a top-level info string) and average the x, y and z values (kostya/benchmarks 'Json' test). Timed region is parse plus averaging; reading the file and the self-test run before the timer. The Serde Typed row is serde_json::from_str into a #[derive(Deserialize)] struct with only x, y and z fields; the C++ rows build a full DOM.
corrections.caveats: 1) Not like for like: the typed Rust rows deserialize only x, y and z and skip name and opts without allocating (Serde Custom does not even store the array), while the RapidJSON and nlohmann/json rows build the whole document; the like-for-like DOM row (Serde Untyped, 0.557 s) loses to RapidJSON (0.154-0.194 s). 2) Asymmetric builds: the C++ flags carry no -DNDEBUG, so RAPIDJSON_ASSERT and nlohmann's JSON_ASSERT stay live as assert() (cost not measured), while the Rust release profile turns debug assertions off; RapidJSON is also built without RAPIDJSON_SSE2/SSE42, so its SIMD whitespace skipping is off on a pretty-printed, whitespace-heavy file. 3) Version drift: the README's Versions table (Rust 1.97.1, g++ 16.1.0, clang++ 22.1.8, serde_json 1.0.150) does not describe these rows; they were measured on 2025-08-17 with Rust 1.89.0, g++ 14.2.0, clang++ 19.1.7 and serde_json 1.0.142. 4) Float handling: the kostya Cargo.toml enables no float_roundtrip, so serde_json parses floats best-effort (an emulation by a wave14 enricher put 1-2 ULP errors on about 35% of the x values and about 10% of y and z); the README's list of inexact parsers names default RapidJSON but omits serde_json, and only the RapidJSON Precise rows (0.212/0.262 s) are exact, so the margin over Precise is not a same-accuracy comparison. UTF-8 validation of the input runs in fs::read_to_string outside the Rust timer. 5) simdjson On-Demand (0.060 s g++, 0.062 s clang++) is about 1.8x faster than Serde Typed and DAW JSON Link (0.085-0.089 s) about 1.2x-1.3x faster (derived from page data), so serde_json is not the fastest JSON option here. 6) Single workload on one machine from a third-party multi-language suite; medians with median absolute deviation. 7) The crate README's claim ('500 to 1000 megabytes per second deserialization and 600 to 900 megabytes per second serialization ... competitive with the fastest C and C++ JSON libraries or even 30% faster for many use cases') carries no table; its linked https://github.com/serde-rs/json-benchmark (archived by its owner 2024-05-20; serde_json 1.0.72, rustc 1.59.0-nightly 2021-12-07, Intel Core i7-6600U; C++ built with -std=c++1z -O3 under clang 11.0.0 and gcc 10.1.0) shows serde_json DOM parse at 320/420/300 MB/s (canada/citm_catalog/twitter), slower than RapidJSON's 380-390/680-890/320-440 MB/s on all three files; DOM stringify is faster on canada (430 vs 200-250 MB/s) and twitter (910 vs 600-870 MB/s) but slower on citm_catalog (560 vs 1090-1650 MB/s); struct parse is 580/710/550 MB/s with no labelled C++ struct column. That Rust harness sets jemalloc as the global allocator while the C++ harness uses the default allocator, the README's RapidJSON table does not say whether its columns are DOM or struct, and the committed cpp/main.cc runs only canada.json (citm_catalog and twitter are commented out), so those rows are not reproducible as committed. 8) serde_json is itself one of the json category's listed baselines.

corrections.workload: Parse a generated, pretty-printed JSON file (json/generate_json.rb: 524,288 objects, each with x, y and z doubles, a name string and an opts object holding a one-element array, plus a top-level info string) and average the x, y and z values (kostya/benchmarks 'Json' test). Timed region is parse plus averaging; reading the file and the self-test run before the timer. The Serde Typed row is serde_json::from_str into a struct with #[derive(Deserialize)] (serde_derive code generation) holding only x, y and z; the Serde Custom row adds a hand-written Visitor through #[serde(deserialize_with)] that sums the array without storing it. The C++ rows build a full DOM.
corrections.caveats: The serde repository itself has no benchmark or performance numbers (its README only says 'efficiently'); the only numbers found are the kostya/benchmarks Serde rows, which exercise serde's derive path through serde_json on JSON text, so this measures serde_json plus serde_derive, not serde as a format-agnostic framework. No comparison against Boost.Serialization, cereal or a C++ reflection-based serializer was found; the baselines beaten (RapidJSON, nlohmann/json) are DOM-style JSON parsers outside the category's listed baselines. Not like for like: the typed rows skip the name and opts fields without allocating while the C++ rows build the whole document; the DOM-style serde_json::Value row (0.557 s) is slower than RapidJSON DOM (0.154-0.194 s). Asymmetric builds: the C++ flags carry no -DNDEBUG, so RAPIDJSON_ASSERT and nlohmann's JSON_ASSERT stay live as assert() (cost not measured), while the Rust release profile turns debug assertions off; RapidJSON is built without RAPIDJSON_SSE2/SSE42 on a whitespace-heavy pretty-printed file. Version drift: the README's Versions table (Rust 1.97.1, g++ 16.1.0, clang++ 22.1.8) does not describe these rows, which were measured on 2025-08-17 with Rust 1.89.0, g++ 14.2.0, clang++ 19.1.7, serde 1.0.219 and serde_json 1.0.142. The kostya build does not enable serde_json's float_roundtrip, so floats are parsed best-effort, as in default RapidJSON; RapidJSON Precise rows are 0.212 s (g++) and 0.262 s (clang++). UTF-8 validation runs in fs::read_to_string outside the Rust timer. The closest declarative, type-mapped C++ comparator, DAW JSON Link, is faster (0.085-0.089 s) and simdjson On-Demand is about 1.8x faster (0.060 s g++, derived from page data), so serde does not beat the best C++ typed parsers on this workload. The same suite and rows back the serde_json record (https://github.com/serde-rs/json) in this wave and wave14's lang:rust/kostya/benchmarks#json, so this record may fold into those. Single workload, one machine.
